body: Nice for a short detour from the beach, I took the bus here from Tangalle. The caves are all quite similar, and not amazing if you have been to Dambulla but still worthwhile due to the beautiful surroundings and lack of tourists.Frescoes in the caves are very nice.
title: quiet

body: Nice quite place to visit; early morning or late evening ( to see sunset) ;do not forget to visit kindergarden; paid guidance is quite simple- do not forget to read info before;
title: Small Sigiryia

body: This is a old Buddhist rock temple. The temple is well kept and beautiful. You have to climb the climb is bit steep.
title: Buddhist

body: We are very independent travelers and are used at organising things ourselves. This temple is amazing with 6 reclining Buddhas in caves that have been painted over 300 years ago. We decided to take a guide at the bottom of the steps to get detailed explanations and history about the sites. Unfortunately we paid 1000 rupees for a one hour tour. This was a total rip off as most guides simply walk you up the steps identifying some trees and giving you little information about the statues and painting. A total waste of money! Do not take a guide, no matter how much you are quoted!Nevertheless, this place is a must-see attraction. Beautiful.
title: Do not take a guide for this visit!!!

body: One of the best place to see in tangalle,view rocks, monkeys paintings ,sculptures are really interesting .must watch temple and very famous place for all tourists who comes to tangalle ❤❤👨‍👩‍👧‍👧🔇⌛️
title: Dumi

body: About 600 steps have to climb. Ideal in the evening to see sun setting in around 6 . Colorful paintings including the Buddha’s stories gives the history of culture and Buddhism.
title: Leisure.

body: This ancient temple dates back to king Dewanampiyathissa. There are four levels. on the top level(4th level) there is a Bo tree( dethis pala ruha bodhi දෙතිස් ඵල රුහ බෝධි ) on the second level there is little pagoda (stupa) that contains sacred relics of Maha Paduma thero (මහ රහතන් වහන්සේ).very calm nature and surroundings. I meditated few minutes on top level next to the Bo tree,very relaxing, you should try too.Highly recommended.
title: Mesmerizing place !

body: excellent ,brilliant place that can to be proud as a sri lankan and it has a great point of view .. in a top
title: Wonder of asian

body: A great place to visit for a short trip from Tangalle. About 30 mins each way and 1.5 hours needed there. I paid 2000 LKR for the round trip including the driver waiting whilst I looked around.There are three levels of little rooms with many big reclining Buddhas and paintings. They were not the most impressive shrines, especially if you have seen similar already, however, I mainly enjoyed the atmosphere of the place. It was so peaceful and the views were spectacular. There were little monkeys running around with some very cute newborns hanging on to their mums. Make sure to go right to the top and follow the path to the back of the highest stupa to head out onto a rock ledge with a marvellous view.The journey itself is also pleasant, past buffalo, rice paddies and lakes.
title: Lovely temple, cheeky monkeys and beautiful views.

body: This temple with all the beautiful paintings is well worth a visit. A place considered holy by the local buddhists, so no footwear, and modest dress. Truly remarkable, but badly maintained
title: Buddhism with history

body: The setting is nice, very quiet place and lot of stone stairs. A beautiful painting in the caves and the view from the top of the rock is beautiful. We did it in the late afternoon to avoid too hot hours. Highly recommended to visit!
title: A Very Beautiful Discovery.

body: It's a nice place to visit, the views aren't at the very top as there's trees in the way which is a shame, but you can see further down. But be warned of anyone welcoming you at the entrance, we fell into that trap and struggled to get rid of the man, in the end we got bullied into giving him money.. That's what ruins visits like this for me. I understand that they get little money, but I do find it a little insulting when you've paid an entrance fee and then there's a person around every corner trying to get you to donate.
title: Nice place, without a guide!

body: Rock temple, very quiet place, a lot of stone stairs. Nice paintings in the caves. Monkeys. Beautiful view from the top of the rock.Highly recommended to visit!
title: Must see

body: Visited the rock temple from Goyambokka beach, all-in it takes about 2-2.5 hrs, only 30 min by Tuktuk from Goyambokka beach (tuktuk price was 2,000 the whole journey). The 600 steps is not as bad as it sounds, visit the site in the morning or in the afternoon. There’s a small entrance fee. Worth a visit.
title: Worth a visit

body: lovely place, you can get an idea about Buddhist culture, amazing arts and amazing view. dont forget to visit this place
title: brilliant place

body: It's a very steep climb so be careful if you have dodgy knees, maybe give it a miss. Great if you're in the area and the drive from tangalle is lovely with water buffalo and rice fields. Tuk tuk cost me 1700 return and he waited which was great. The views from the top are the best part but the wall paintings are pretty too :) not amazing but worth the trip if you're looking for something to do in the area
title: Worth it if in the area

body: Mulkirigala Raja Maha Vihara (also known as Mulgirigala Raja Maha Vihara)is an ancient Buddhist temple in Mulkirigala, Sri Lanka. It has been built on a 205 m (673 ft) high natural rock, surrounded with another four rocks known as Benagala, Kondagala, Bisogala and Seelawathiegala. Its so hot during day time, but its worth climbing up.
title: Complex of temples on a rock.

body: Ancient Buddhist rock temple that is definitely worth the visit if you are around Dikwella or Tangalle. Constructed on top of approx. 200m high rock (challenging climb), lots of statues and cave paintings from 3rd century. Also impressive view from top of the rock (you can even see Ella from there). Very low entrance fee. Best to climb early morning or before sunset. Covering knees and shoulders necessary (sacred place). Carry some water with you (can be bought next to entrance).
title: Ancient rock temple with amazing views

body: You must go if you are located in Tangalle. It is only 30 min from Tangalle. The parking costs 30 LKR (if you come with your own vehicle). There are lots of vendors at the parking. You can buy water and some snacks. First, you pass the school yard and just before the first two cave temples, there is also ticket office (500 LKR/person). The area is not maintained, but it is a worth a visit. Some steps are pretty steep but there is a fence almost all the way to the top. We went today at around 10AM (sunday) and it was not crowded at all. Our 2 and a half year old almost made himself to the top. The walk is not hard at all. The ride from Tangalle takes approx. 30 min (one direction) and we spend cca. 1 hour there - with walking, taking photos,...Make sure you cover your legs, and you need to take off the shoes every time you enter into one of the caves. We wore running shoes.The view from the rock is amazing. It is a perfect mix of Sigiriya and Cave Temples in Dambulla (only less crowded and less steps :) ).
title: Great morning trip

body: Situated in down south in a beautiful area , this rock temple has four levels . Very attractive images .Make sure you climb to the top were it is like a heaven.
title: One of the memorable places in Sri Lanka

body: Located about a 30 minute drive from Tangalle, I ventured out here early in the morning to avoid the heat of the day. To my surprise, when I arrived 9am I was the only one there. It's similar to other places I had visited in the Hill Country and the view from the top is non-existent, however the hike up was refreshing and rewarding. Worth the visit.
title: Interesting Place

body: It's a very nice and calm place out of the bitten track. Personally I loved these old steps carved into stone and these old rocks covered with flowers and lianes more than the temples themselves. On the way you'll see almost nobody except for monkeys. That's a great advantage compared to Dambulla. Well worth visiting
title: Very beautiful

body: Well, we visited the temples as we were in the area and were travelling from Tangalle to Ella by taxi (Senu Cabs). I knew that we would not have enough time to visit Dambula and I also read that Dambula was much more crowded with tourists. You can bet that Mulgirigala has a very local character and that is what I liked. The temple might not be that grandiose as Dambula but for me it was much more important to see the local spirit here.You´ll see monkeys in the trees. Right from the beginning a local guy was trying to accompany us but as we knew he would ask later for some money, we told him right away politely we would not need a guide and he accepted it without any insisting.
title: Instead of Dambula

body: Mulkirigala Raja Maha Viharaya consists of a series of rock temples carved out of the face of a huge rock during the second century B.C. There are about 53o steps to climb to reach the top. I can still remember the spectacular view from the top when i visited here 20 years ago, but that view is now obstructed by overgrown trees and bushes. The caves have a number of beautiful paintings and sculptures.
title: Rock cave temple, worth a visit

body: There are lots and lots of steps, many of them steep and slippery after rains. But it is worth it to climb all the way to the top and out on the ledge to have a great view of the surrounding countryside.There are three grottos with large Buddha statues where you will need to take off your shoes. Do also check out the little monkey bath area off one of the grottos.It took us slightly over an hour to reach the top, with mini excursions into the different rooms on the different floors. There are toilets at the base where you will need to pay 20 rupees, but it has a tap outside to wash up.There are also stalls selling drinks and coconuts etc at the entrance, so you can refresh yourself after the climb.
title: Well worth the climb to view the Buddhas and the surrounding countryside

body: Mulgirigala (also called Mulkirigala, or Mulkirigala Cave Temple) is located northwest of Tangalle and north of Dickwella. This little-visited cave temple complex became our favorite Cultural/Archeological site in our 3 week exploration of Sri Lanka. (We also loved the Cave Temples at Dambulla). A 600-foot granite monol;ith with five different levels of cave temples connected by 533 steps. The caves, dating back to 1st and 2nd century, house massive reclining Buddha, scores of other statues, and remarkable wall and ceiling paintings. Visiting this combined with a visit to Wewurukannala Temple (Sri Lanka's largest sitting Buddha statue) makes for a greast half-day excursion from Tangalle or Dickwella.
title: Also called Mulkirigala. Little-known, but One of Best Cultural Spots in All Sri Lanka

body: Went to see these while in Tangalle. They were ok bit not great.Some interesting depictions but very minor compared to the amazing cave temples in Dambulla. Cost 500 LKR to get in which is not a lot. The walk up to the top was the most interesting part but even from the top there are no views of the surrounding areas.
title: Ok, but not great.

body: Really amazing , not too much steps. Perfect if you have children Must visit in case you didn’t visit sigiriya rock
title: Amazing

body: There are a lot of stairs to climb but it's worth it. Many people only make it to the first level but take your time and get to the top. The three caves have amazing paintings part decorative and part telling morality tales. Don't miss the third small cave with a painted cobra on a door at the back. Monkeys play all around the site.You can get a blessing from the monk on duty at either the top or lower level.
title: Make it to the top

body: Good place with historical value. Hiking and best to go morning or evening time because of the sun light. I saw monkeys on my way.
title: Rock hiking

body: This is the most wonderful place in srilanka. The colourful painting are really attractive. You must visit here and enjoy with good vibes.
title: Attractive place

body: Nice temple with some great artwork in the caves. If temples are your thing then definitely go there, though if you did the rock temple in Dambulla then this one might not be different enough to be worth the trip out of Tangalle. The views from the top were mainly blocked by trees which was a shame. Decide before you go up if you want a guide, since they will follow you and talk to you quite persistently without telling you that they will eventually want money.
title: Nice place

body: Mulgirigala temple caves were first built in the 3 century BC;built on a 205 m (673 ft) high natural rock, surrounded with another four rocks known as Benagala, Kondagala, Bisogala and Seelawathiegala, the temple site is located about 2 km (1.2 mi) from the Mulkirigala junction and can be reached from either Dikwella or Tangalle towns. With its beautiful frescoes is a must if you stay in Tangalle and nearby areas.From the top you can have an amazing view until the southern coast, spacing from the paddy fields and the lush coconut plantation.
title: Astonishing rock cave temple with beautiful countryside surrounding

body: You'll need to climb 565 steps to get to the final room at the top of this temple. Each room is beautifully decorated with well-preserved paintings. The view from the top is amazing. Well worth a visit.
title: Lovely paintings and amazing views

body: It may have been just luck but we where basically alone when visiting this gorgeous rock temple at sunset... the perfect amount of steps with little kids (we have four from ages 2-7) and our local guide found at the entrance to the temple was truly wonderful. We highly recommend this visit especially if you can’t make it to the more popular rock temples near Kandy. We recommend arriving around 5 pm to catch the sunset from the top of the temple overlooking the gorgeous surrounding jungle.
title: Best of the beaten path excursion

body: This place is wonderful one. we got good experience with attractive vibes. Huge of trees and colourful paintings. one of the good place to guests and we recommended
title: wonderful

body: This is an incredibly moving visit. The temple is on multiple levels, with many shrines to Buddha. All very accessible but still (from a totally secular perspective) interesting, notable and fascinating!Great monkeys and the most incredible views from the top.Worth the 600+ step climb!Don't miss it...
title: You have to go! It's amazing.

body: This place is really amazing! The paintings are really impressive and the landscape is beautiful! There are some steps but nothing too hard. Lots of monkeys and around 5/6pm we saw the local people praying which was also something beautiful. I recommend this visit!!
title: Amazing!!!!

body: The temples are really worth a visit. The landscape is incredible with lots of rocks, palm trees, lush forests. Climbing up, you have an amazing view. The temples have gorgeous murals. We went there around 5/6 in the evening so we could see the monks chanting while hundreds of monkeys played in the trees.
title: Beautiful temple in a beautiful landscape

body: The spot is worth a visit to see this ancient buddhist place of worship built into a massive rock. A few steps to climb. A lot of art and sculpture to see. No shoes and respectfully dressed
title: Ancient HHistory

body: Mulkirigala was part of a half day trip we made in the area of Tangalle. You should take some water with you (as well available in front of the monastery). The walk up to the Buddhas requires to climb up on stairs which are chiseled in the rocks. To be honest compared with thai temples not that spectacular but fascinating as well because it must have been extremely hard work to build that. And this is the Sri Lanka style of showing their deep faith. Therefore a must do to get a sight into the culture of that great country.
title: Impressive and worth to visit

body: Decided to visit the Rock temple with my boyfriend yesterday afternoon and it was absolutely stunning. The frescos are breathtaking as much as the view from the rock. The guide was great: he explained us the meaning of the frescos and the statues, he led us to the rock and he also took amazing photos of us. We met with two monks who blessed us on our way to the top. It was quite emotional.The guide also gifted me with a bunch of fresh frangipani!
title: SPECTACULAR

body: We have decided to go for a trip at the last minute and left Tangalle at 5pm. Arriving to the temple at 5:30pm was a bit late but when we hiked up the stairs, the last visitors were leaving which left us the temple for ourselves. We took the guide who provided interesting information about the temple history. Views from the very top of the rock were magnificent. We even got the blessing from the monk up in the rock and children were able to ring the temple bell - amazing experience.
title: Scenic views uphill, absolutely non touristic

body: We spent a couple of hours here. Fantastic place. No problem getting up on the top of the rock even though the 500 steps. The view is amazing.
title: Worth the trip

body: Worth the 500 steps. Make sure you see the view from the rock at the top. Watch out for monkeys. Beautiful temple. And don't be fooled. You don't need a guide.
title: Rock temple is amazing at sunset

body: This is a monastic site with temples carved out of a rock outcrop. The climb to the top comprises about 400 steep steps with little reward at the end. It appears to be a little neglected and the view at the top is partly blocked by trees and other vegetation. Unless you have a passion for temples don’t bother.
title: Not worth a stop

body: Worth a detour and 500 LKR each if you're travelling south from Ella to Tangalle. You won't need a guide so tell them early!!
title: Interesting Buddhist rock murals

body: ... in the backcountry of southern Sri Lanka. Even the short busride (from Beliata) through the countryside is worth the trip. The buddhist statues, the 200m high rock and the great view from the top is a wonderful half-day trip after some beach days at the coast
title: Magic spiritual place

body: Me and my partner visited this temple with high hopes. We got a tuk tuk there and back from tangalle for 1500lkr which we thought was reasonable. Upon arrival we were greeted by a nice man who started to guide us around the temple - foolishly we assumed he worked for the temple and was part of the entry fee. This was not the case and he asked us for 1000lkr once we reached the top, not a large amount but a bit annoying. Similarly there are a couple of people around who offer you a 'blessing' by chanting as they tie a piece of string around your wrist, for a price. I don't have anything against receiving a blessing but they should at least try to keep some sort of act of sacredness going rather than calling friends on their phone immediately afterwards. In terms of the temple, it was ok, quite a few rooms with statues and paintings in, but nothing out of this world. The views from the top are similarly mediocre, with most sides being blocked by foliage.
title: It's alright

body: This Temple was The surprise of my Sri Lanka trip. I have seen many Buddhist temples in my life but this one beats them all. The temple dates from the 3rd century and was further developed during the centuries after. It contains some stunning wall and ceiling paintings dating to over 350 years ago. It's one of the few archaeological sites in Sri Lanka that are not overcrowded with tourists and if you are lucky you will be receive the special blessings of a monk in a short ceremony. The temple has been built on a 205 m high natural rock and you need to climb a 500 step stairway to reach the top. The stairway leads you to different platforms with in total 7 cave temples where you can relax so it's not that bad. You will have stunning views of the surrounding mountains just behind the temple on top. Definitely worth to visit.
title: Beautiful temple and stunning views

body: There's a climb up a steep hill to get to the caves but they are worth it. There were only about 7 other people when we walked around. The caves are filled with ancient paintings on the ceilings and walls and have a number of Buddha statues. We were suitably impressed with that. However, we didn't spend too long at the temple, as you can take the most of what it has to offer in a fairly short amount of time, I'd say it's worth a visit if you're in the area. We found the place much calmer and quieter than some of the other tourist attractions. So remote.Stunning views would be provided if you have a little walk around the small temple on the top and find a cliff top.You won't be able to refuse to het some coconuts to drink on your way back (Rs100/pc).Entrance fee is Rs500/pax. Dresses and shorts must cover the knees as it's a temple.
title: Fantastic countryside views from the top

body: A great place, but they should start now saving it from manmade damages and rubbish. It isngetting worse each year i visit it. But is still an impressing encounter with old buddhist culture. Do not miss it before they have to close it for some reason.
title: They must save it now!

body: It is absolutely worth a visit. 600 steps to go to the top. My problem: nothing is explained. The signs tell you only what is forbidden, not what you are seeing. Spectacular view from the top.
title: Nice, but

body: We visited on a Sunday morning and the temples were fairly quiet. On arrival we were bombarded by flower sellers, guides and even a demand for a parking fee (very enterprising!). We went in and paid a nominal fee and walked round alone. So much nicer if you want a peaceful visit, Even inside the complex be prepared for some assertive guides/sellers. The temples were stunning, with wonderful statues, frescoes and artwork. Wear good footware for the steep steps, you can leave them outside each temple. Overall a very special place well worth visiting.
title: Spectacular cave temples

body: Nice and peaceful templeThere are lots of steps to reach the sommet of the temple but it worth it !!!!expecially if you are so lucky to meet a monk who will give you the blessing of Buddha!!!!
title: Peace

body: A little off the tourist path. Historically nice with a large number of caves with sleeping Buddha's. 500 Rupee entrance. Lots of business making people inside. Sad that the place is not well maintained.
title: Lacks maintenance

body: This place is an (almost) secret delight. The cave temples here are more beautiful than those we saw in the cultural triangle and were so peaceful with hardly any visitors mid-morning. The climb up provides two levels of rock temple and a small temple at the top. A little track around that temple brings you to a cliff top with stunning countryside views. This is a gorgeous place and easy to visit on a three wheeler from Tangalle. Very highly recommended.
title: The most beautiful temple we have seen in Sri Lanka

body: you get that feeling that the visit to this historic temple makes you feel like a traveller who is not looking for something ordinary. the "little sigiriya" as its also known is a historic Raja Maha Viharaya where the bo sapling planted was one of the 32 from the original Ficus Religiosa. constructed in the 3rd century, the temple is located on top of a boulder (200m high above sea level) and was built by King Saddhatissa
title: A historic temple off the beaten track.

body: The temples and views themselves are amazing and understandably one of thee most popular things to see in Sri Lanka. Don’t miss it!Sadly, it has obviously become a way to weasel a lot of money out of tourists, and the 1-hour visit become unnecessarily expensive. The 500lkr entrance fee per person is more than fair, but only half way up the cliff did our tour guide (that we never asked for) tell us that he would cost 4,000 rupees on top of this and that it was compulsory to buy flowers to give to Buddha and to donate money at many other points of thee tour. The tour itself was not at all informative (here said about 3 sentences just over and over again and then pointed at the viewing spot, then said the tour was over). It might sound a bit tight! But we’ve had some amazing and highly informative tours around temples in Sri Lanka which were included in the entrance price (for which we would then have the choice to give a tip at the end, which we always would!), and the quality of this tour, in hindsight, made this feel like quite a scam.
title: Amazing landmark, to to be missed — unexpectedly expensive

body: We got a tuk tuk hear from Tangalle- for 1500 SR return trip. There is a bus that's an even cheaper option. We choose not to have a guide and wandered around in the early morning enjoying the ambience of this tranquil place. The steps are plentiful and my husband elected not to go to the top level. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Definitely worth a visit.

body: Sometimes the thought of yet another temple is just too much. I was so pleased I visited this one. No crowds, beautifully serene location, fantastic surprisingly beautifully painted caves..... just wonderful and a blessing or two if you want it. Can easily get here by public transport and thereafter a short walk
title: Fabulous

body: must visit this ancient place if you are visiting Tangalle ! you can learn lot about culture of this great nation , do not forget to get guide , can learn lot .
title: great journey

body: This temple complex is really beautiful,cut in to the rock side.7 caves which are all adorned with artefacts and huge tombstones.Reasonably easy to get to with public transport,a good day out.
title: Well worth the visit

body: An awe-inspiring place, not only of theological interest but also of great historical significance. The complex is only a short drive from Tangalle and was relatively quiet when we arrived around 10am on a Saturday. You need to have a decent level of fitness to ascend as there are some steep climbs involved thought the ascent is broken up into stages. Guides loiter near the entrance and charge 2000 Rupees to show you around. They aren’t university level trained but give you a flavour of what you are looking at and I’m sure the money is very welcome and a small price to pay to support their livelihood. The caves contain some stunning illustrations dating to over 350 years ago. The jungle setting is very Indiana Jones. We consider ourselves pretty fit so the ascent wasn’t a bother, and spent about an hour and a half here which was ample time to wander and take it all in. An excellent treasure to discover for anyone visiting South Sri Lanka.
title: An archaeological wonder in the jungle a short drive from Tangalle

body: If you’re in the Southern province, a visit to the cave temples at Mulkirigala is recommended. Spread over five terraces, there are a total of seven temples, each with its own story. The moment you step out of your tuk tuk, you’ll be surrounded by people wanting you to buy their lotus flowers but we didn’t begrudge the 100 rupees as it’s expected to give an offering. The steep climb adds to the drama of the ancient site but it’s hard going on your bare feet. We noticed others had not deposited their shoes at the ground floor entrance as we did, but kept them on and just removed them when entering the actual temples. This place is reminiscent of the rock temples of Dambulla and located on and in a huge rock similar to Sigyria but pales in comparison. When you reach the very top, you can climb down onto a rock platform to get a great view of the surroundings. Some of the temples were not as well looked after as they should have been and there are areas with bags of rubbish heaped up- not something you expect on a holy site. On the whole it’s worth a visit.
title: Like a mini Dambulla

body: We arrived here from Tangalle beach to take a break from the sun. It was a lovely morning trip, only 20km from Tangalle and possible to arrive by tuk-tuk. Amazing to see more than 2000 years old caves temples paintings!
title: Beautiful temples off the beaten track

body: It was nice sightseeinng. Lots of monkeyes. Nice view point up on top. About 7 caves nicely decorated with natural coloures in traditional way.
title: Skalní chrám

body: We were amazed by the giant rock. It resembles Dabulla but caves are located scattered. Paintings are in superb condition. Photography allowed. Small amount has to pay as entrance fee. Dress code as usual to other religious places.
title: Please spend some time

body: Maybe it was the guide that couldn't speak english that well or maybe there was really nothing to see, but i thought that it was nothing special. At first the guide wanted 10$ for the 30 minute tour. When we refused the price dropped to 1000 rupies for two persons.Theres only 3 rooms to see and every room ise the same.Look at the pictures online and you'll get a better tour than on the spot.
title: Nothing special

body: The place is around 18km from Tangalle and you can get there easily by bicycle or local bus.There are a few cave temples in the rock on three levels. Beautiful wall paintings inside the temples.To reach there you have to climb the rock however it is not demanding as stairs are available.The view from the top is nice, palm forests and mountains, however a bit obscured by the trees.Entrance fee is around 3$.
title: Nice place with cave temples

body: Definitely worth visiting this beautiful 2000 year old cave temple in the jungle if you are in the South
title: Beautiful cave temple in the jungle

body: The temple caves were OK but the best part was the view from the very top. We recommend to go be there when the sun is setting
title: Amazing view from the top

body: Interesting setting on a huge rock There are seven temples in different levels. Climbing more than 500 steps is a challenge. Final steps are more challenging. So remote. Less tourists. Architecture comes close to Sigiriya rock. Lovely paintings on the walls as well as on the ceilings.Magnificent views from the rock behind the dagaba. Better to start early morning or late afternoon to avoid bright sun.As this is a temple , make sure to wear decent clothes . Not forgetting comfortable shoes.Definitely a must if you are in Tangalle area.
title: Unique Cave Temple

body: If you've seen other Bhuddist Temples and places of worship around the world, then this is not on the must see list.After paying the RS500 entrance fee and being reprimanded to take your shoes off before entering the places of worship, it's a 15 minute climb to the top of the rock.Along the way you will be pestered by tour guides (not needed) and hawkers that sell anything from food, water to souvenirs.Be reminded to dress appropriately, knee-long shorts and a short sleeve shirt for men is ok, women need to cover their legs down to the knee, a sarong type skirt is suitable.The area is not very clean and has a run-down appearance. No need to spend more than an hour here.
title: If you're in the area....

body: This is a fascinating place. Well worth the visit.Go early in the morning to avoid the heat and the crowds.
title: Early morning trip.

body: Lovely place to visit; big temple complex with a beautiful view from the top. Needs some attention in places because it has some minor maintenance issues. Our guide took us outside the perimeter stone fence to show us an even better view. Watch out for the lovely but cheeky monkeys.
title: Amazing view!

body: Found this temple in our guide book and was a good stopping off point between Unawatuna and Udawalawa National Park. Definitely worth going to. We were met by a guide, Sampat, who showed us all the levels of the temple. Good English and 1000 rupees well spent. Cost a few rupees more as we went up the various levels with voluntary contributions to the people who showed us specific details. Very interesting - absolutely stunning view from the top. Like Dambulla caves, although not as old, and much, much, quieter.
title: Worth visiting.

body: Very interesting but the grounds needs some money spent. A bit rough around the edges. Watch out for the monkeys. Don't take any food. You can get a blessing for a small offering which is nice.
title: Worth the effort for something different

body: We went to the Mulgirigala Temple in May 2017. Being the low season we were the only ones there! Upon parking our tuk tuk we were immediately approached to pay a parking ticket although we were parked on the road. Then to buy lotus flowers. On walking into the entrance you are met with the most magnificent Rock, and it truly takes your breath away. On the right there is a small museum with the most incredible artifact"s from hundreds of years ago. We were then approached to be blessed, this is where a pray is said and a white cord is tied around your wrist. There is a scared hat used and when this was raised we noticed a LRK 1000 note, which actually distracted the energy from what would have been a sacred moment for us. We were then asked for a donation and was met with a stare of distain when we only gave LKR500.We then approached the first steps and stairway to the first level. There are 5 levels and 7 caves. Yet again we were asked for LKR 1000 each and given a ticket that looked like a raffle ticket. To be honest we were not that amused as we were in a Buddist temple and everything is my a donation that you choose... we began to feel like we were "taken for a ride" when we really wanted to immerse ourselves in the splendour of the place.Once we finally did start climbing the stairs, (it takes around half an hour to get to the top) we went into the caves on each level and it was amazing. Why?...because it was quiet and you could feel the history and feel the immense sacred energy we felt blessed. The lying Buddha is unreal and it was so good to just "be" and really take it all in.Each cave is wonderful and if you are there when it is not too busy you have the opportunity to take a while and breathe it all in.We reached the top and apart from the litter etc...the view is wonderful. We had other friends visit and they said that there was a path behind the top level with the view, we found it just slightly below the top over to the left side.All in all it was well worth going to and because of the "Rock" and the nature around it all it cannot be missed. body: It is a really beautiful tuk tuk ride from Tangalle. I highly recommend taking the tuk tuk as you get to see the beautiful area. We visited twice. The first time there were many monkeys on the walls and we got to enjoy the entire area with no one else. The monkeys were not aggressive. The second visit we went and the monkeys were all having a swim. It was awesome! I loved watching them run and jump and play. There are many stairs but it is worth the effort. There is a beautiful view at the top. THere are many little caves with numerous laying buddhas. You can break up the hard climb! Bring your own water! There is a little shop at the bottle, near the entrance.
title: Great place to go and we loved all the monkeys!

body: A visit to Mulkirigala is worth a visit, though you travel deep into the rich interiors. also known as the little Sigiriya due to its imposing boulder and steps leading to the summitthe paintings and ancient, religious scriptures are fascinating

body: We met Sampath outside the temple, asking us if we needed a guided tour - we didn't know anything about the temple or history, so we said yes!He was a great guide and taught us a lot - we could ask any questions along the tour and he would gladly answer them. The temple is nice itself, but we wouldn't have liked it as much if it wasn't for Sampath! He stood outside the temple by the small stands, just before you enter the temple. We would highly recommend him as a guide!!Sampath phone number is 0774388589

body: This is a verry important place for the buddist,also travellers this is an old temple..come and enjoy natural world

body: It's called mini Sigiriya due to the similarity of rock structure. But like Dambulla, it is a Buddhist temple containing 7 painted caves. Initially we thought it might be just like Dambulla, but after visiting both, we found that frescoes are different in nature. Specially in Mulgirigala, Dutch influence is very easy to notice. Travellers interested in ancient paintings are advised to visit both Dambulla & Mulgirigala.We visited Mulgirigala during a Poya(full moon) day and were fortunate to see special rituals performed by local people. It is really a memorable experience.
title: Different from Dambulla & Sigiriya

body: What a fascinating place! Go early to avoid the heat of the day when climbing all those steps. Our guide was wonderfully informative and great with the children. We were blessed by a monk at the top and were asked to ring the temple bell. The girls were entranced. The view from the top was magnificent. Well worth the visit and 500lkr per person entry. 30 mins by tuck-tuck from Tangalle.
title: Fabulous

body: I been there couole of days ago,,its rocj temple brst view arround tangalke and really calm place,try it and look arround vilkage area
title: Clean place

body: Really nice temple with 400-500 steps to the top. Our tuk tuk driver, Manoj, has explained to us all the important about meaning of each caves, which was very nice. You can relax on the top, just follow little path behind the temple. Nice morning trip from Goyamboka for 1800 LKR.
title: Nice cave temple with beatifull view

body: This was amazing! Fantastic way to spend a few hours! You don't need a guide, it's easy to read about the history in advance and then find your way up the paths and steps amongst the cave temples. Make sure you have some change to buy lotus flowers as offerings to Buddha on the way up. I was dressed covering my knees and shoulders but other women were in hot pants so I guess it is at your own discretion as to what you wear. Flip flops were fine, but there are some steep very worn steps in places. Make sure you have plenty of water too! Views at the top are stunning! We saw many monkeys and beautiful plants at the temples too. A great way to spend a morning. Unfortunately a guide approached us at the bottom of the temple and we said yes.... once at the top he asked for a huge sum of money. Lesson learnt! It would have been much nicer to go at our own pace. He was on his mobile the whole time too. Everyone else we met in Sri Lanka was genuinely kind and helpful though :) I would go back to visit the rock temples and caves at Mulgirigala again.
title: A must see!!

body: We spent an afternoon with Sampath as our guide and he was amazing. We have three very young children and he helped get them to the top in a safe way. He was extremely knowledgeable and fun. We would recommend him to anyone.
title: Tough but fun

body: Climb to the top of the mountain, when you go around the side, and there's a beautiful view of the sunset.
title: Very nice sunset

body: Be prepared to hike 500+ steps while exploring the 7 caves! As this was a last minute, end of the trip excursion, we departed late morning, but in hind sight we probably would have fared better heat/humidity wise had we gotten an earlier start. Nevertheless, we survived and fortunately were well-stocked with water to replenish what we were sweating away. We made this trek with our three children (12, 10 & 6) and they held their own without issue — zero dramatics. My youngest nephew (3) hitched a ride on his dad’s shoulders so this definitely fulfilled any gym work that he might have missed out on while on vacation. The four yo managed just fine with occasional guidance, especially on the overlook boulder with quite the drop. Our tuk tuk drivers were kind enough to arrange a guide for us on our arrival — the little unexpected ambush of the surprise guide was well worth the extra money. The scenic views and swimming monkeys were an added bonus, as was being blessed and getting to ring the bell.
title: Wonderful cultural experience

body: Definitely worth a visit esp if you miss Sigiriya and Dambulla - it's a mini version of both rolled into one. OK not as impressive but still very interesting, quieter and not as expensive. Scramble behind the stupa at the top for great views.
title: Worth the climb!

body: Thoroughly enjoyable experience made all the more interesting by the onsite guide, Sampath, who took the time to answer questions in a way that the children could understand.
title: Excellent guide

body: Impressive rock temple. Quiet. Not many visitors. Man at temple on top will advise you where you can take amazing panoramic pics!
title: Worth a visit if you're in the South!

title: nice site. disappointing clerk

body: Would definitely recommend visiting this amazing Buddhist temple if you are in the area. A secluded location, it is worth visiting in the latter part of the day to avoid the hot sun. Definitely climb to the top to get the best views, and enter the caves to see the amazing cave paintings and Buddha statues.
title: Beautiful buddhist temple

body: This was described to us as "temple ruins", but as it is still in working order, and houses monks, I would not really describe it as such. There are three different levels, which are accessed by quite steep stairs. Each level has a lovely view over the countryside. There are also lots of monkeys scampering around. They don't seem to be bothered by humans. It was interesting to see how the temple had been built into the rocks, with the rock making the walls and ceilings, and then beautifully painted. We paid for a guide, 1000 rupees, but I don't really think a guide is necessary, as it's quite a self-explanatory layout.
title: Lovely paintings, not really ruins

body: Lovely place to visit, a lot of stairs to the top, the various rooms are split over 3 levels, mostly similar in each room. Unfortunately some of the Buddha are behind some old glass cases. The site could do with a good tidy up, our guide didn't have the best English but was fairly well informed. Definitely a lot of scope to improve the site.All in a good visit that's worth doing if you don't get the opportunity to see other similar sites. Tuk tuk is probably the easiest way to get there but it's a long way off the beaten track. It's fairly inexpensive too.
title: Lovely cave paintings and sleeping buddhas

body: We visited the temples from Tangalle and spent 1.5 hours in them. The temples are nice and so are the multiple reclining Buddha in the caves but it's nothing out of this world. You can get there by hiring a tuk tuk but I'll cost you between 2000-2500 ruppes. Instead, go to the bus stand in Tangalle and get a local bus. Just ask around and people will tell you in which bus to get on. It only takes 45 minutes and costs 45 ruppes. It's very easy, don't waste your money in tuk tuk.
title: It's ok

title: A beautiful and peaceful visit

body: A monastic temple carved out of a rock outcrop comprised of four terraced levels. There are several rock temples with Buddha statues and wall and ceiling murals. Some date from 2C BC while others are more modern. It's a bit of a climb up with some challenging rock carved stairs to be careful on but pleasant as you can rest at each level while enjoying the temple and the terrific views over the lush country side.
title: Wonderful Temple

body: Nice spot. It's ramshackle version of dambulla, with excellent Buddha caves, a little off the beaten track.I normally like steps, but these were the wonkiest I've come across so far in SL. Safe but the unevenness breaks your rhythm and stride. There is a fork just below the top level with some steps hewn into the rockface, the alternative is a flight which almost folds back in on itself.There was a pond at the top which the monkeys were using as swimming pool.Now the caves, all similar in style, there were some images with what looked like halos, there were some airborne folk on clouds, and there was something resembling a nativity scene?There was a very enthusiastic chap at the top chanting mantras for my GF, with a fee 1k rs notes around as a hint.There was a strong cooling breeze at the top which was lovely and possibly brought about by the chants.As we were leaving a guy rushed over top charge out driver a parking fee....hmmmmm?
title: Temple of the wonkiest steps!

body: We did this as a morning trip from Tangalle. It was really interesting and we got there relatively early and there were very few western tourists. There are quite a few steps between each of the cave temples but its not too arduous and the view at the very top is superb....great swathes of coconut palms all around. The cave temples themselves are full of buddha statues and wall paintings similar to those in Dambulla but not as good. It's still well worth a visit and very interesting seeing the local customs and the listen to the atmospheric buddhist chanting.
title: Nice trip from Tangalle

body: Less popular than its cousin Dambulla in the north, this is not full of westerners (saw one other couple on my visit) Small entrance fee of a few hundred rupees plus going rate of 1000 rupees for english speaking guide. Paid 100 rupees for 2 lotus flowers to offer to the Buddha. The buses stop on the main road in the village and the temple is about 15mins walk along the road (signposted)The guide was very friendly and knowledgable but didn't really tell me anything I couldn't have read in a guide book. He was very handy to take pictures as I was travelling solo that day, and the company was nice.This temple is not for the faint hearted or vertiginous, the steps are very steep and uneven in places, but he was happy to wait while I rested on the way up. Don't miss the herbal tea and sugar lumps that the ladies sell between 1st and 2nd level.The Buddhas and cave paintings were stunning, so colourful (if a little dusty!) Don't miss the cobra cave with its cobra cupboard! Remember to remove your shoes when entering but don't go wandering about outside without them as the stone floors get VERY HOT!I couldn't find either of the ancient stone inscriptions, and my guide had left me at the top without pointing them out.For those that can make the top the view of the lush green countryside makes the effort worthwhile (most people climb around the wall and onto a huge stone ledge for a better view!)Don't forget to make a donation and get a blessing from the monk at the top (for a safe trip back down again perhaps)There has been some effort to address the problem of litter, with a few dustbins placed on the levels, but there is still some rubbish around, but generally the site is cleaner than most places I have seen in Sri Lanka.Definitely worth a day trip if you are staying in Tangalle/Dikwella/Matara area, or passing through on the way elsewhere.
title: Off the tourist trail

body: Steep, challenging climb but well worth it. Book a guide to explain all about the temple. Get to see monkeys on the way up.
title: Breathtaking view at the top

body: Breathtaking views, but you have to work for it. Our guide seemed very knowledgeable about the temple and its surroundings. We gave him 1000 rupees. He patiently waited for us throughput the ascent while we caught our breath or took pictures. Fantastic views of the surrounding landscape and the Buddhist and Hindu statues and paintings are magnificent. Bring small rupee bills or coins for donations along the way up and be prepared to spend 200 rupees on lotus flowers as you arrive for an offering to Buddha. We also enjoyed seeing the monkeys and monks in training. We were a bit shocked by the amount of garbage strewn about the site or would have given a 5 star review.
title: Great Local Experience

body: It's very beauty full place, Rocks, Trees, Monkeys are take my all bad feeling and I forget every moment being there. green jungle trees every way around me. step by step I climb the rock then top of there is a Buddha. with me lot's of local was too. but there are so friendly and smile with me. very nice evening sunset are there.
title: I saw beauty with natural rocks !

body: It is one of the best temples complex I have been visited. There is few floors, Temple buildings, big white stupa, monkeys, monks and Buddha's statues. I really recommend it!
title: Beautiful and magical place

body: Very interesting place.You have to climb many steps.The view from the top is amazing. gems garden arranged a tuktuk for the return journey to Milkirigala ,costing around 1500 rupees. It was amazing .....
title: "VERY NICE TEMPLE"

body: I love the Mulgirigala Rock temple. I've been to Tangalle 3 times and it's the one temple I visit each time. It's a little way out of tangalle but so worth the trip. The inside of the temple is stunning and the view from the Rock is breath taking. On my first visit I was there while the monks were chanting. Sorry but I don't have the words to explain how beautiful that was. The next visit was over Vesak poya day so it was busy and fun and well worth the experience. Then there is the comedy show if the monkey playing in the tank. All sizes and ages enjoying cooling off in the water.
title: Serenity and monkeys

body: It is easy to see why this is the number one thing to do around Tangella. Absolutely amazing! A guide will greet you as soon as you get out if your vehicle and they are difficult to shake. We paid 1000 rupees (which seems standard) and didn't really consider him worth the money. His English wasn't great so we didn't learn a whole lot. It was also hot and he was quite keen to discourage us from walking the final 150 steps to the top (where there is no cave). The "tour" was also done at lightening speed. On the way down we we asked if we could keep looking around, at which point the guide left us, making for a much more relaxing visit!So, if you can, ditch the guide and enjoy looking around!
title: Pretty spectacular

body: Very nice tempels, fee tourists and stunning views (if you walk all 700+ steps).Buddhist monks are on site to bless you whilst putting on a bracelet (in exchange of donation).
title: Our first temple in Sri Lanka

body: Very interesting place. You have too climb many step but the experience is very high! We did with our daughters of 4 and 6 y.o. without any problems. The view from the top is amazing. Is half an hour far from Tangalle.After this visit you can jump in to the water in the blue paradise beach at East from Tangalle...just 20 minutes from there.
title: Family trip

body: Brilliant place to visit. The walls of the temples are breathtaking and providing you can manage it up the stairs, the view from atop the Monastery is something very special. Would implore you to seek guidance from one of the guides who work there.
title: Fantastic Insight

body: The climb up is about 500 steps of varying hight and steepness. Intermittently, there are temples that provide time to regain your breath and enjoy the views. In July the view from the to is limited, as the green trees hide the views. Do buy a bunch of lotus flowers at the gate to donate to the Buddhas. Also if you are not a Buddhist. It gives something extra to the experience.
title: Resonable climb with impressive Buddha statues

body: This is a lovely monastery with an excellent views of the surrounding country side. We got a tuktuk from tangalle which was about 1000 rupees return. Entry was 500 rupees per person. Worth it for the view from the top alone. You'll get a 'guide' that will attach to you as you get out of the tuk tuk. We paid 1000 rupees to ours which was worth it as he knew where to see the nice views and had a little knowledge on the temples themselves. (You need to be fit to climb the stairs)
title: Nice monastery, with a great view

body: Buckingham Place arranged a tuktuk for the return journey to Milkirigala, costing around 1000 rupees if I remember rightly. It takes around 45 minutes to get to the temple. A guide was arranged for me and I am cross I cannot remember his name - he was so good he deserves to be publicised. All I can remember is his name began with S and he lived a few hundred yards from the temple. He guided me through the whole experience and as a keen photographer, he was able to tell me where to get the best photos and had the knowledge to be able to use my complex SLR camera to take pictures of me. I made sure I went late in the afternoon, arriving about 3.30, to miss the highest heat of the day. I am a reasonably fit 62 year old and had no trouble with the steps, though they certainly made me sweat! The view at the top was superb and well worth all the effort. Make sure you stop to see the monkeys playing in the trees and on the rocks before you set off down the steps.
title: Very impressive paintings and statues for a ridiculously low price of 500 rupees

body: If you are ready to climb more than 500 steps you will enjoy one of the best views of the south coast from the top of the rock next to an historical temple.
title: Ready to climb?

body: very interesting temple very very old with a fantastic amazing view a lot of momkeys burds i saw bats river with lotis fglowers and nice sunset
title: ver nice temple very old and tiryung to arrive but the view is very amazing spettacolare

body: We booked through the Hotel and it only takes a few hours. Late afternoon when not too hot. Quite a few steps to climb !
title: Good only if you need to get away from the resort

body: This monastery is accessible to people of all fitness levels. The total number of steps is in excess of 500 but it is broken up into manageable sections with views and smaller shrines along the route.An 'official' guide attached himself to my wife and I and we negotiated a price of 1000 rupees. We were glad we paid for the guide as he really did enhance the experience with his knowledge of the history and the best places for photos. The monastery also charges 500 rupees per person at the foot of the stairs. We were initially a bit put out about the price but after realising that the whole thing, with a guide comes to about £10 we became a bit more relaxed about the whole thing and decided to just enjoy it. The shrines themselves are breathtaking as are the views from the top. This has been one of the highlights of our trip so far and is worth every penny.
title: A step above the others!

body: This old rock monastery is a bit off the beaten track for most travelers, but if you happen to be around, it's worth a visit. If you're approached by a guide at the entrance, debate with him the price upfront, to avoid problems at the end of your tour. Make sure you don't miss the view from the rock just behind the top temple.
title: Go for the view at the very top

body: Dambulla is probably the best known Cave Temple in Sri Lanka,probably because it is in The Cultural Triangle and on the main road.However,there are many similar sites across this amazing island,and Mulkirigala is a good example.Just a short drive on a good road from Tangalle it is well worth a visit.No tourist coaches means that you can explore at your leisure. There are several hundred steps involved,but quite manageable. I am 68 years old with a crook knee,but had no trouble. There is a small museum at the entrance,and then you proceed up to the caves. There are 7 caves over 2 levels all containing interesting statues and paintings. One cave has a bit of Hindu influence. If you are feeling fit you can climb more steps to the top where the stupa is located and be rewarded by a majestic 360* view of the surrounding countryside. Well worth the 500 re entry fee
title: Better than Dambulla and without the crowds

body: this is overprice entrance, its more like mini Dumbulla. Not that much worth to visit if your on a budget. I went by public bus and walk 200 meters from main highway and climbed for 20 minutes to reach the site.
title: overhype,expensive

body: Interesting place with amazing views from the top. Be warned you will be met by a " guide" at the entrance check the cost of his services before you head off. You then pay an entry fee and are asked for a donation every time a monk blesses you. The cheapest thing is the refreshing king coconuts at the stall out the front when you get down.
title: Lots of steps.

body: less touristic than many other temples, it's worth a visit5 floors of ancient painted caves carved in the rockOne of the most amazing things we've seen there
title: great visit outside Tangalle

body: This is like a little Dambulla in the South of Sri Lanka without the huge amount of tourists; We arrive there at early morning (9 am) and were the only tourists, with only 2 or 3 locals. When leaving the site one hour later 2 groups of tourists just arrived!
title: Go early at the morning

body: Mulkirigala is quite small and not as popular as other monasteries in Sri Lanka, but still it's a great place to visit. Several stupas and shrines on top of a cliff look beautiful and offer wonderful views. This is not a place to visit after you've been to Sigiriya and Dambulla, but it's a good place to start your acquaintance with Sri Lankan places of interest, especially if you are staying in Tangalle. When you are there, try the crazy stairs - you'll know what I mean when you see them. They are not as difficult to climb as they seem to be, but thinking that you have done that is a nice memory to have and to boast of.
title: Try the crazy stairs

body: If you've climbed Sigiriya's Lion Rock, you can probably skip this one. It's a gentle climb up steps to a temple at the top. The art work on the roof and walls is intricate, and the views from the mid-level is the best. An old man will say a prayer for you while wrapping a string around your wrist, though you'll be expected to leave a monetary offering - just a few hundred rupees - and there's another guy up the top who'll do the same if you feel like you need more than one prayer a day. If you're in the area, and you're at a loss for something to do, it's worth a half hour (on top of the 20-odd minutes to get there).
title: A Very Mini Lion Rock

body: nice trip, nice monastery,we liked the paintings /murals and the climb up the hill to overlook the area. Especially nice was riding on the elephant
title: impressive monastery

body: Such a historical, spiritual place - be sure to get a guide to guide you up the stairs and take you to the amazing outlook. It should only cost you 1000 LKR and well worth it!
title: It's amazing

body: We went there from Rekawa which took about half an hour in a tuktuk. It is similar to the temples at Dambulla except that the temples here are on different levels as you walk up the rock. We were there just before it opened (about 7.25) and so it was very quiet and peaceful. We liked the fact that we were able to be in the temples on our own which made it a wonderful experience. The old temple keeper was a very kindly man who pointed out interesting features. Although we couldn't speak each other's language we managed to communicate. I would highly recommend it. The little cobra temple was particularly fine.
title: Wonderful visit

body: A nice half day jaunt from Tangalle or anywhere along the Southern coast. You could go by tuk-tuk, but better go by bus: first to Beliatta then to Mulkirigala. The bus will drop you about 1km from the site and you can stroll along.Interesting cave temples hewn into the large Rocky outcrop: gaudy to the western eye, but full of life in the paintings of gods, disciples etc. also two large Buddhas.Some steep steps, but handrails and no real feeling of vertigo!
title: Poor man's Sigiriya / Dambulla

body: No magical atmosphere here... Everything looks worn out and in very bad conditions... Although open to be visited by tourists the facilities are so poor that looks like you are visiting a suburb rather than a temple. Avoid
title: A bit disappointing

body: This is a great place to visit if you are staying nearby. It took our driver approx 30 minutes to get there. There were lots of monkeys and the temples were beautiful. Takes about an hour or so to get up and down. There are some very steep steps at the top.
title: A beautiful piece of Buddhist history

body: Beautiful environment with large rocks, you'll be surprised here. come and see this historical place. relax your mind. domestic and foreign visitors.thank you.
title: Tangalle to Beliatta via Mulkirigala Rd, Older than 200 yrs,

body: This rock temple is about 30 minutes from Tangalle and perfect for a morning trip. Entrance fee was 500 per person and we paid about 1500 for the tuk tuk trip (not sure about the bus connection). At the beginning, there is a tiny museum room which you can easily skip (I think they wanted to charge 100-200 for it). You could get a guide as well but you do not need one if you have some time to walk around and explore for yourself.There are a lot of steps to get up to the top, and some of them are very steep, but there are places on the way up where you can get a break from the stairs (e.g. the rock temple). It was rather hot when we went, so you should not forget your water, but there were only very few tourist but mainly locals visiting the temple (and a lot of monkeys), so dress appropriately. If you get to the top, it is surrounded by trees and bushes and you have to get over the stone "wall" at the back and then down a small path through some trees to get an amazing few of the surroundings.Overall, we actually preferred it over Dambulla as Mulkirigala has fewer tourists and a much more spectacular way to get up.
title: Nicer than Dambulla

body: Nice and very detailed art on the walls, amazing view from the rock - go there in the evening when it is about to close. We were there pretty much alone at around 5:30 / 6 pm just before it closed. Amazing!
title: Go there in the evening

body: This is an interesting and well kept temple with lots of wall paintings and Boeddha images. It gives you a good idea how Boeddha spent his life. It is easily accessible by bus from Tangalla
title: Temple

body: the beautiful rock temple at Mulkirigala is about 16-18km away from the Tangalle town and approximately 20-30 minutes drive. the temple has rich history and dating back 2000 plus years, this ancient temple has many caves with Majestic yet relaxing Lord Buddha statues and at the top there is a Chetya. you will be climbing about 600 step to go to the top and its worth going there and in 1830 at the British colonial day in Sri Lanka George Turner had found the Great Mahawansa (great Cornical of Sri Lanka) all the historical Kings were written down here, and the excat cupboard that they found the book is still there,best time to go to the place In the evening where you can see the beautiful sunset at the top off the 290m high rock.
title: Rock Temple...

body: It was a great visit. An interesting Rock Monastery with caves and a lot of wall painting. Not recommended for elderly people and for those who have mobility issues. Breathtaking views when you reach the top. Interesting important Buddhist site. Worth visiting.
title: Great visit !! Interesting !!

body: We arrived early @ 9am to climb all the stairs. There were very little tourist at that time and temperature was not peaking. at several places along the climb one can stop to visit a sanctuary and catch your breath. These caves are nicely decorated, although some are restored rather unprofessional. The whole are seems rather neglected, dirty and wasted. It does feel more like a neglected touristic attraction than a monastery.
title: Impressive but rather wasted

body: We visited the rock temple which was about a 45 minute drive from Tangalle. The temple has a few different levels which you have to climb up (around 700 stairs I think although not too challenging) which have different Buddhas to visit. The view from the top is stunning! It is advised that women are covered up however I was given a wrap to wear.
title: Rock temple near Tangalle

body: Better to visit in the morning, the rock isn't so hot. You have some 570 steps to go up to the stupa! Must see!
title: Great place!

body: Wouldn't get a guide!! do spend time enjoying the peace...not busy especially in the morning.Beautiful place better at the top
title: Walk to the top

body: Having been to Sigirya etc we thought that we had completed the "must do" list in this lovely island. However, already bored after a day on the beach we made the short trip from Tangalle, not expecting very much. I am so glad that we did as the paintings on the walls and ceilings of the caves as well as the reclining Buddhas are wonderful. The climb up is quite hard work in the heat and the granite burns ones bare feet but well worth the effort. The entry is only 500 LK which is very reasonable, especially compared to Sigirya. The view from the top is obstructed by vegetation and it is worth climbing down to the big rock at the back to get a lovely view. There were lots of young monkeys playing in the water when we were there - a delight to watch.
title: Well worth visiting

body: After reading about Mulkirigala, we asked our guide/driver if he recommended a visit. He had never been there but was game to try it and so we made a detour on our way back from Yala to Galle. We got there around 9am and were the only visitors around so we had a nice tour with the monastery guide Rowan. It is a steep climb of 550 steps but you stop in small temples at different levels so you can catch your breath. I managed despite my vertigo (there are at least railings everywhere) and even my ten-year-old daughter was able to make the trek with the help of our guide/driver. We were all sweating quite a bit by the end despite it not being very hot.The frescoes are really beautiful though not original (they are roughly 200 years old though the site has housed temples for purportedly 2000 years). The views along the way are great and the carambola tree on the way to the top level was stunning in bloom. There was also a playful family of macaques a few steps down and behind the top temple. Be sure to buy some lotus flowers at the bottom if you would like to leave them as offerings in the various temples. At the top you can receive a special blessing from one of the monks in a lovely and brief ceremony if you so desire.
title: Nice detour on way back from Yala

body: If you havent been in Sigirya, Dambula or similar rock temples. Otherwise I dont recommend because it is nothing special.
title: Good

body: Nice trip from Tangalle for about half a day. Take a bus from Tangalle to Beliatta and then ask for the bus to Mulkirigala Junction Bus Stop. Then you can take a tuktuk (100rs) or walk about 15 mins. Worth a visit!
title: Nice trip from Tangalle

body: A very interesting temple to visit but be prepared for a lot of steps. Recommend you pay for a guide as they are very knowledgable. Take the effort to get to the top as the views are fantastic.
title: Well worth a visit

body: Visited this monastery when we were holidaying at Tangalle. The drive from Tangalle city took about 45 mts by car. To climb the rock takes about 30 mts only. The art in the cave and the view from the top is absolutely stunning.
title: Mulkirigala monastery

body: We had heard a lot about how peaceful and serene these rock temples were a- our expectations were easily met. The 550 steps mean you need to be averagely fit and avoid the heat if th day but the cave temples make the climb worth while.Certainly worth a visit.
title: Serene

body: This was a nice excursion accessible by local buses. The scenery surrounding the temple is beautiful. At 500 rupees it is an affordable activity in Sri Lanka. Unfortunately many of the Buddhas in the caves are under old glass cases. The site could use some more maintenance but it still made for a nice climb up the many stairs.
title: Nice visit

body: This place has 3 levels to you reach at the top... 2 levels had Buddhist temple, last one has monastery ..last climb was difficult owing to small rock steps, but it was great experience. We climbed in afternoon with no tourist around, and enjoyed ourselves thoroughly.. Entry fee is LKR 500 i believe, and it was worth the cost.. This place is recommended only if you have some time, and you staying nearby..
title: Walk through the trails...

body: We visited this temple at 9am and there were very few other tourists. We expected to make a donation or to pay a small admission fee but it turned out there were a lot of hidden costs. As soon as we got out of our tuktuk a guide approached us and insisted on taking us around the temples. Stupidly we did not ask how much this would cost... He was mostly chatting on his mobile & was really in a hurry. At the top he demanded 1000 rupees. The other tourists we saw had no guide so I would definitely recommend that you make your own leisurely way up to the cave temples and say no to them at the start. We had to make donations in each cave temple (we were unprepared and didn't have any small money) and also pay an entrance fee then for parking at the end! However, it's well worth climbing the 589 steps to see these ancient rock temples. Some parts are a steep climb but there is a railing. I managed in flip flops. We saw a lot of monkeys too! The art work is a beautiful mix of Hindu and Buddhist imagery and it's one of the most interesting and peaceful places we have visited on our trip. There are stalls to buy water/snacks at the bottom.
title: Worth the walk

body: Really nice place a lot of steps but the view is worth to going at the top of the temple. Additional attrastion was lot of small monkey.
title: Worth to see

body: well worth a visit if you are nearby - about 500 steps to the top - once you get there the view is breathtaking and on the way up enjoy the beautiful cave temples and buddhas and paintings.

body: We went there 16.00 and where almoast alone. Climb to the top adn reach the backside where theres a cliff with excelent views. The budhist on the top is also more friendly than the others.

body: Not something to do in the heat of the day . This is definitely a place to visit in the evening. The paintings in the caves look like they have been restored but it is defiantly worth a visit. The view from the top obstructed by trees but nevertheless sunset was beautiful
title: Beautiful and inspiring

body: Great place to do meditation and worth the climb up if really like nature and temples. After climbing to the top look for the foot path which leads to a rock from which you have some beautiful views of the surrounding areas. The medicinal tea is worth a try after the climb.

body: A smaller version of Dambulla rock temple in the north. However the 584 step climb is definitely worth it. Take a guide he will cost you no more than LKR 1000 or £5. But if you're interested he will talk about Buddhism and the rock temple all the more. Once you get down after your visit to the temple, visit one if the ladies at the stalls and try a cooling drink of "wood apple" juice. Very nice and refreshing!! Entrance fee LKR 500 each

body: Nice paintings and sculptures with brightly colors in a nice country side. Peaceful place with not so many tourists. Just not so much view on the top.
title: Nice paintings and sculptures

body: This temple is about a 30min tuk tuk ride (25km) from Tangalle but is definitely worth visiting if you are in the area. Make sure you go in the afternoon as any other time and you'll be out in the hot sun.At the entrance there is a small museum, which is quaint but probably not worth the visit. If you ignore the caretaker and proceed up the stairs you'll reach the entrance - Rs500 per person. When you arrive you'll also have lots of people trying to sell you flowers for offerings and there will be an occasional guide selling his services. I think that it was better and more relaxing to explore this site on your own.You then climb more stairs to a group of rock caves, need to take of your shoes & hats and women should have their legs covered - for a small donation you'll receive a blessing & a white string bracelet. Climb the stairs to the top and there's a small temple - which for another small donation you get another string bracelet. The rock caves all have Buddhist shrines, which immediately remind me of the rock temple at Dambulla but only a fraction of the people - when we were there, there was just over half a dozen people visiting the entire site. The caves have numerous statues of Buddha and amazing murals on the ceiling. The stair climbs are reminiscent of Sigiriya but there is only about 500 steps so it's not too strenuous. The views over the surrounding countryside is equally impressive. It is one of those few must visit places if you are in the area - you'll be pleasantly surprised at how beautiful and unspoilt it is.
title: Serene, Spiritual - An Amazing Temple on a Rock Hill

body: Peaceful temple that climbs a rock wall - each level has different rooms with buddhas and other statues. Not too difficult a climb until the very end (steep and narrow steps) but there are a lot of steps. Not super crowded, and we ran into more Sri Lankans than tourists, which was nice.

body: Rock monastery was decent value, there's a 500 RS charge per person and 1000 for a guide but I think this is optional. That adds up to S$20 if I'm not wrong. Lots of steps, bring water, interesting stuff to see and great views/photo ops from top.

body: This is an ancient temple pilgrims are climbing this to warship and as a hobby.this is fill with ancients arts

body: Off the main roads and beaten tracks, we recommend going here in the afternoon, when the sun is not so hot, as you'll climb a lot of stairs. There are I think 7 cave temples, mostly small, but given you'll be mostly alone there, it's much better experience then in crowded Dambola, for instance.If you can, avoid the first guy right after the gate, it's a Buddhist "museum" not worth it, he'll rush through the exhibits with close to null English, will push you to get a white string around your wrist and require donation for it. Then you'll have to pay the entrance fee later anyways, so just avoid it :) There will be another guy offering the white string on top again, if you really want it.

body: Visited mulkirigala early morning.very calm and quite at the moment.great ancient place with ruins.itwas take about 10-20 minutes to take the peak.better to visit with suitable dresses as this is buddhist nonstary.

body: great paintings in caves and far less touristy then the ones in central sri lanka. worth a visit, just make sure you are ready for the steep steps up! fine for us but we saw a few older couples who were a little out of breath!

body: Enjoy the many steps up the mountain (+/- 560). The views of the surrounding area are excellent. The history is incredible and the art painted on the walls and ceiling must be witnessed to be appreciated.

body: Note...the location of this specified on TripAdvisor is wrong, so I'd suggest checking on Google first!! We took the public buses from Tangalle as others have suggested below.... (Both about 15 mins long). It was great fun, and easy to do too... Better than a tuktuk. When you make it to the top, be sure to find the secret rock view just behind the courtyard wall and trees.... body: This place is a little hidden away but absolutely wonderful. There are three 'levels', connected by steep stairs, containing rooms in the rock with sleeping Buddha’s and stunning Muriel’s on the ceiling. The rock itself is gorgeous, and it's definitely worth climbing to the top for the amazing views. Top tip, when you get to the top climb over the wall and check out the views! We sat on the mountain top and a family of monkeys came and sat with us – a truly wonderful experience! Also take a big bottle of water,it’s a long way to the top but definitely worth it!The rock itself is gorgeous, and it's definitely worth climbing to the top for the amazing views. You need to remove shoes and hats to enter the rooms, but it's more correct to climb the entire thing shoeless if you can.It was very quiet and peaceful when we visited (about 3pm on a Saturday) and the climb isn't too arduous. There are few touts either, so the whole visit can be quite relaxing and tranquil and is a fantastic way to spend an afternoon.
title: Stunning and easy to walk around

body: Save some money and go by bus! Starting from Tangalle to Beliatta, change to bus to Mulkirigala. Locals and officials will help you find the right one. Costed us ~50 Rs. per Person and took about 45 minutes. Compared to Tuktuk (read about 2-3000 Rs!) It's a bargain!Then just 1000m by foot and you're there.At the beginning it seems unspecular, but with every cave it gets more impressive!Right on top we got a blessing by a local who also recommended us a short way to a point with a spectacular view Over the jungle! Worth a Visit! Entrance is 500 Rs.

body: This place is situated near to Beliatta. Better way to reach it from Tangalle is by bus, it's cheap and quite comfortable. Bus is cheaper and all local people can help you to find right bus at bus station.Temple is really big and beautiful. By the way you will meet monks and they will give you a blessing for small donation (~100 Rs). On the top of monastery there is place where you can enjoy fantastic view.

body: Good if you like your templesBit of a walk up steps not suitable if you have walking difficultiesHad a guide but felt would have been better on my own not very helpful

body: We were staying in Tangalle and visited the temple on a rainy day. The temple and surrounding area is quite beautiful but some areas of the temple are worn down. body: 500r each to get in. And the place is pretty run down for that.You basically walk up a million steps looking at some quite cool rooms built into the rock, then get to the top and the trees are massively over grown and you can't see anything.Then a guy stings you 50r for parking outside.

body: We had been to both Sigiriya and Dambulla, but thought that this temple was definitely worth a visit. It is more rustic and less commercialised than other places, so you really feel you're visiting an authentic location. The uneven steps, cave temples and spectacular views from the top make this a delightful place to visit.
title: amazing temple, worth a visit.

body: When U plan visit Tangalle or south of Lanka, MUST SEE!!!Colorfull temples in Rock.Step py step U can discover caves wih temples...Unforgettable
