body: a hidden temple only locals know about , small dambulla , beautiful scenery from the top, very helpfull monk in the top temple
title: hidden temple with panoramic view from the top

body: This place is a little hidden away but absolutely wonderful. There are three 'levels', connected by steep stairs, containing rooms in the rock. All of these contain amazing wall and ceiling murals and some very impressive statues. On the first level is a ticket office, staffed by very friendly individuals, and the price is only 500LKR (about £2.50)The rock itself is gorgeous, and it's definitely worth climbing to the top for the amazing views. You need to remove shoes and hats to enter the rooms, but it's more correct to climb the entire thing shoeless if you can.It was very quiet and peaceful when we visited (about 3pm on a Saturday) and the climb isn't too arduous. There are few touts either, so the whole visit can be quite relaxing and tranquil and is a fantastic way to spend an afternoon.A few tips and things to watch out for: You can jump off a bus on the Beliatta road, but you have to know exactly where (the sign is quite easy to miss) in order for the bus to stop in time, plus after a certain point in the afternoon the buses are very few and far between. We opted to travel to Tangalle (3-4 hours from Galle via Matara, 2-3 hours direct bus from Galle) and then got a tuk tuk, which took us there, waited and then drove back. It was only 1700Lkr (about £8.00) and the drive itself is a lovely trip through winding countryside.On arrival, someone will try and sell you flowers. These are offerings for Buddha and only cost 50LKR. You should wash them at the sink provided on the first level before offering. Also, as you start climbing, a man will join you offering to be a guide. This isn't free. Agree a price beforehand if you want, but in my opinion, it's much nicer to take your time and explore alone. He isn't overly pushy and will leave if asked politely. Lastly, a few monks on the ascent will offer a blessing for 100LKR. They tie a bracelet around your arm and bless you. It's quite a lovely experience and worth, I think, the price.All in all a great visit and great chance to relax away from the hustle and bustle and tourist touts of the more popular tourist destinations.
title: Steep climb but very much worth it!

body: Great place to visit, very quiet and calm. Very old religious site with interesting statues of Buddha with wall and ceiling paintings.

body: A bit hidden in the hinterland but can easily be reached by tuktuk or even better with private motorbikes. Entrance fee is 500Rs now, but compared to other sights still pretty cheap. Its quite a climb up the few-hundred steps, avoid going in the midday heat.

body: Mulkirigala Rock Monastery is a beautiful site which has a historical value hidden in it. The climb was not that difficult. Caves with lovely wall paintings and amazing statues. body: the Mulkirigala Rock Monastry is situated in a quiet and serene location which immediately takes you back few centuries in time. body: It is very nice and historic budha temple. We saw here a lot of beautiful budha statues and paints. I can recommend for tourists.

body: Patrick and Angelina from AroundSriLanka.com Tours & Excursions took us with their tuktuk to this place, it is like a mini Dambulla, absolutely stunning! There were monkeys swimming in the pond, the cave drawings are beautiful and the view at the back of the top temple is just mindblowing! We were the only tourists around and we have been sitting on top of the rock for about 45 minutes with nobody else around, only the sound of the birds and the view of the nature... must see!
title: Not touristic yet absolutely stunning!

body: A smaller version of the Dambulla cave temples. A nice walk up, good for all ages - our guide was 80! Children can take it at their own pace. Beautiful artwork, peaceful, and interesting. I definitely recommend having a guide, his stories and explanations really made the visit special.
title: Beautiful - a must see in Tangalle!

body: Definitely an historic attraction, and while enchanting and enjoyable it was a little unkempt. Impressive nonetheless and worth the scooter trip and 500r entry fee. Good views from the top. Make sure you climb the barrier at the top and walk out onto the rock, just don't fall!!
title: Ok

body: This was a must to visit on our journey through Sri Lanka. It is a steep climb up to the top of the hill. A guide will join you to show you around. He is not free. Settle price before you go up. Fantastic paintings and statuary. Loved the blend of Hindu and Buddhism
title: A must to visit

body: Wonderful old Buddhist temple with seven caves decorated with paintings and statues. Beautiful scenery and a Nice walk up the many steps to the top of the temple with great Nature and a Nice View.
title: Wonderful Buddhist Cave temple

body: The Mulkirigala monastery, or the "rock temple" as the tuktuk drivers call it, is recommended in the lonely planet book. We went there, and were not disappointed! I guess its not the best and most interesting monastery in sri lanka, but if you're in Tangalle area it's a nice option for a sightseeing. This 3 levels monastery contains a few huge laying buddha statues, and many other wall statues and paintings.Many many stairs lead the way between the levels, so be prepared to sweat quite a bit! Entrance fee for turists: 500R.Best way to get there is with tuktuk, and you can also combine a visit to the Wewurukannala Vihara "big buddha monastery" in Beliatta.
title: Interesting monastery, tough climb

body: A nice place on top of a rocky area, caves are nice but not as impressive as in Dambulla, the environment is quite nice, not too many tourists, we had a local guide but I am not sure you really want to have one, maybe it is better to enjoy the quite atmosphere of this place alone.
title: Nice visit off the beaten track

body: We were advised to see this temple area by the host of the guesthouse we stayed. A awesome find and well worth a visit. The area of I suppose Christian equivalent to hell'" was a bit confronting, but you do not have to go into that area ! Paintings and plasterwork excellent.
title: A little Gem

body: Magical temple complex on a hill. Very quiet later on the day during off season. Only a few euro's entrance fee.
title: Because we did not visit Sigirya and Dambulla we went here and thought is was wonderful.

body: A hidden secrect. Very quiet place, almost no tourists. Could be better maintained, but the view from the top of the rock is great, a lot of stairs to climb to see the caves with the buddahs, but worth a visit.
title: Little secret

body: A mini version of the more well-known Dambulla cave temples. Nevertheless, the interior walls are beautifully painted with pictures of Buddha and other characters. The climb is manageable. Visit early in the morning and you will have the entire place to yourself most of the time.
title: Beautiful wall paintings

body: We read the reviews on this monastery before we went so we knew what we were in for. I really don't know why the lady shoved flowers in the tuk tuk as soon as we pulled up because she was the only one selling them and the guide was painful too, giving out unwanted advice before he offered his services, we decided not to use the guide. We entered the gates now on our own and found the friendly ticketing office and we were on our way. 500lkr per person. The caves are on two levels, left of the ticket office and the ones on the right, we decided to do the climb on the right first. The stairs are generally small and steep but there is a thin railing to hold on to. The cave is in good condition, there are 3 rooms and a man outside the first who seemed to be selling guidebooks. When we exited the man asked us if we wanted a bracelet, for 100lkr as he wraps the material around your right wrist will chanting a blessing and sends you to the Buddha Room on the right. After visiting the room we discovered more steps.The next climb took us to the stupa at the top of the rock, the views are ok, covered by trees and nothing but trees in the distance. From here we found direct stairs to the midway point, hold on to the railing because it is steep and I had to put my feet sideways on the steps (thankful that I wore my running shoes). The rooms near the ticket office are almost on the same level as the office (3 steps) and right behind the office so you should do it (we had children who said they couldn't walk any further but this was doable). The monkeys were in the trees outside these rooms while we were there. The steps near these caves also take you to the toilets down below (all squat type).We purchased water from the vendor in the car park, nothing cold though. There were only a few people visiting the monastery on the day we went so it was pleasant and the caves are in good condition.
title: Interesting Monastery

body: Took the morning off the beach to explore Mulkirigala, really worth it. The cave temples have some very old, very intricate paintings and the whole site was very atmospheric.
title: Nice painted cave temples

body: We've paid 500lkr per person and . We had a local guide that we've paid extra (1000 lkr). It was a good move, since we didn't know much about the culture, especially about symbolism used in beautiful Budha statues, and it was easier to get around. The monastry looks great and it also has a beautiful view. We haven't been at the top, I was too tired to climb, but I'm sure the view is even nicer.
title: Very peaceful and calming

body: lot of climbing but there is proper steps.a very calm place.may be some times not easy to find the place.but worthy to visit.
title: ancient temple very calm and rich with history.

body: This is a fantastic and beautiful temple 13 kms away from the Tangalle. Dont miss to visit this place. Also you can climb nearly 300 feet along the rock and it was a nice attractive journey. At the top you can see a very panoramic weave
title: Explore Sri Lanka

body: I liked the traditional aspect of this place but didnt like the money grabbing car park attendant or the flower lady. Lots of monkeys around and lots and lots of steps. Great views from the top
title: Interesting

body: Definitely worth a visit if you stay in Tangalle as a change from the beach. This is not exceptional but the site is nice and we enjoyed the climbing of the numerous steps and the atmosphere.
title: Worth a visit

body: Presently this is called "Mulkirigala" but there were several other names such as "Mulgirigala", "Samudda Pabbatha", Muhudu Giri", "Giriba Vehera" "Giriba Lena" etc., etc., You will find seven Cave Temples in five terraces in different heights, Lower Terrace, Bo Tree Terrace, King's Temple Terrace, Upper Bo Tree Terrace and Chitya Terrace. During the time of "King Devanampiyatissa" the Bo Tree Terrace and the Upper Terrace was done. Passing the Bo tree you can reach the lower terrace with two caves. One is called " Cobra Cave Temple" which supposed to be built in 1800 AD. There is a large Reclined Buddha statue inside the cave. Walls were painted with the pictures of "God Saman", "God Kataragama" , God Vibhishana" etc., Also the roof was painted beautifully with Buddha's pictures and floral designs. Next cave is called "Paduma Rahath Temple". Inside this cave too there is a large Reclining Buddha Statue. Then you reach the next cave with " Buddha Parinirvana Statue" which gives the last moments of "Gauthama Buddha". It also displays statues of grieving Bikkus, Gods and also the king. In addition to that there are paintings on "Distribution of Buddha Relics by Drona Brahmin" The path to top most Terrace has two routes, made by cutting the steps on the rock itself. Although it seems to be very difficult to climb the rock at fist, with the help of the hand rail it is exciting. The highest level of the rock gives an excellent view and very quite, calm and peaceful environment, it is advised to climb the rock in early morning or in the evening, then you can stay and relax for a while. Since we climb it in day time it was very hot and we wanted to come down soon.
title: The Rock Temple in Mulgirigala

body: I arrived here around 10 in the morning and was the only tourist there. There a a few rooms were they have some really nice wall paintings, very beautiful in fact. I walked the 300 hundred or so stairs to the top to be blessed by a monk (for a donation of course). There is not much of a view from the top unless you climb down a bit and stand on a large rock, even then there is not much to see. Well worth a visit though.
title: Worth a visit

body: We hired scooters from our hotel and rode up into the countryside to the temple. It was a great way to spend a morning in Tangalle and the temple is pretty impressive. The view is spectacular. Just don't go at midday!
title: Nice break from the beach

body: The site consists of five or six caves around the side of a large rock, each containing a Buddhist temple with large Buddha statues and beautiful paintings and decoration on the walls and ceiling. Apparently the cave temples date back to 400 BC but most of the paintings didn't look that old - perhaps restored. There is a shady car park and a toliet block at the base of the rock, then a couple of hundred steps takes you to the pay gate and the first pair of temples. Beyond that there are another 300 or so steps to get to the top, with more temples on the way. Some of the steps are steep and narrow but there is always a handrail. The rock has trees and shrubs growing on it so there is shade for much of the way. At the top you can walk round the temple perimeter to a rock ledge that gives great views over the surrounding forest and plantations.While we were there, on a weekday morning, there was only one other group of tourists there and we only saw another couple coming in. So the site was quiet the whole time, which meant you could hear the birds singing and enjoy the peace of the temples. A local offered to act as our guide but we didn't feel we needed anyone, and his English wasn't that great. A couple of black eagles flew over the tree canopy quite close and my husband also saw a crested hawk-eagle in the distance.
title: A beautiful place to visit

body: Really nice sight, do take the effort to walk up.Suggest not to make use of the local guides, as not very good English speakers and hardly any info shared ( 100 lkr) . You are better off if you read about the sight before/after .Flowers can be bought close to the entrance outside (for 50-100 rupies) , suggest to take them and offer to Buddha. Stair really steep, not impossible though. You can get a blessing for a donation on two levels even, on the way down fresh coconut milk (for 100 lkr.)The whole sight and scenary is very nice, pity so little information available on the premises.
title: Beautiful, but challanging walk

body: Lot of buddhist and hindu pictures and statues.Entrance is paid 500lkr per person.You can have guide which will charge you 1000lkr or more.Lot of interesting things to see and learn in monastery and beautiful view on the top of it.Monastery is actually built in rock which is very interesting.Only minus is really LOT of stairs to the top of it.
title: Nice monastery with sleeping budha

body: We enjoyed this for the $50 total cost including driver, entrance fee and guide. We drove from Tangalle first thing which is a great idea as it is a bit of a work out and the cooler temps were a help. The caves are interesting, but the rock and view is the best. Make sure you go outside the wall at the top and walk to the east out onto the rock outcrop. Pretty scary as it drops straight down but view is amazing. Unless your "guide" speaks your language, and appears to have some knowledge, save the 1000rupee fee. Ours was mildly annoying but he did show us the secret trail at the top, so worth it in the end.
reviewer: The Fraser Rivers Edge B&B Lodge
title: Very interesting, great views

body: Hotel organized a trip her and have to say we were not disappointed. Our guide was very knowledgable and really wanted to share his knowledge with us in a friendly and engaging manner. Beautiful site and off the beaten path
title: Informative and interesting

body: Especially, if you don't have the time to visit Sigiriya, this rock temple is worth a look. Go early morning or late afternoon as it can be a tough climb in the midday sun - superb views across southern Sri Lanka. Could do better with toilets, rubbish & tourist information in English
title: Worth the trek

body: Mulkirigala Rock Monastery is about 30 mins from Tangalle. There is a nice 20 min walk up the summit and some smallish caves. But the monastery pales in comparison to Dambulla.
title: Decent Attraction

body: There are competing treasures here - the stunning walk round the back of the top temple and the cave temples; a little musty but brightly coloured and beautifully painted (a little like Dambulla but on a smaller scale). It's a bit of a trek to the top - not too bad - but maybe tricky if u can't get up stairs that easily. We loved it - and when we went there's hardly anyone there!
title: Amazing views from the top and lovely cave temples

body: Mulkirigala is a fantastic place. Having visited Sigaria and Dambulla , I would place it only just behind these world class attractions. The climb is steep but interesting with 4 separate cave temples at different levels and the rock painting is wonderful.If you are staying on the south coast and want a break from the beach hire a tuk tuk and make this trip, a great morning out and some good exercise
title: Unmissable

body: This rock monastery, like many other Srti Lankan monasteries, has an admission charge. At Rs 500 per person it is a little steep, as are the 500+ steps up to the top of the rock. It is easily accessed by bus or Tuk-Tuk from Beliatta. The bus drops you off about ten minutes walk from the entrance to the monastery. Apart from the steps there is nothing special about this place. Chambers cut into the rock house statues of the Buddha and many wall paintings. A blessing is available at the summit.
title: An average tourist attraction.

body: Lots of interesting history. The bat cave is a must to see. Also, the paintings inside temple are well preserved. Fantastic views from the very top.
title: Lovely views

body: Get one of the more experienced cab drivers to guide you snd you will have an amazing visit. Without a guide the place is not that attractive since its history needs to be told. Try to go there during one of the festivals.
title: A good days cardio and a great view.

body: You should totally visit the rock temple! If you have the Chance to get a guide, you should spend the money. Due to buddhist culture it is not only beautiful to see the wall paintings and sculptures, the most interesting is the background knowledge to understand. If you walk up to the rock, you can enjoy a wonderful view you should not miss!Don't forget to be respectful and do not pose backwards to buddha for pictures and put on appropriate clothes!
title: Culture at its finest

body: We were Staying in a villa Called Ranna House, in Tangalle. It was a nice 40min Drive from the Villa. A truly Beautiful Villa. Our Butter Kumar arranged for us to visit this Ancient Temple. Well worth the trip. it's a excursion from Ranna House. The climb to the top was a challenge! But exhilarating and beautiful. The frescoes are like Sigiriya. See the culture.
title: Ancient Culture meets Budhist Monastery! WoW

body: quick trip from Tangalla- small entry fee and forced donation later up the steps!Rock temple smaller that Dambulla - just as interesting and much quieter.
title: no other visitors

body: This temple is in Beliaththa . We liked the beautiful paintings on temple walls -The Cave temples consists of Reclined Buddha , Seated Buddha and Standing Buddha Images, paintings of Buddhas, Arhaths, Gods and Jataka Stories.
title: rock temple

body: If you're in the area, definitely worth the trip. We went by bus from Tangalle (one quick change, 30 mn overall one way for Rs. 35) and then paid the Rs. 500 entrance fee each ("donation"!!!).It's a very nice temple in the jungle, carved in the rock. Be ready for some steep climbing, a lot of steps, but the caves are rewarding with old paintings, giant Buddhas and several rooms to explore.Only slightly annoying things are the constant donation boxes (20 scattered throughout the site, would Buddha approve when you've already paid the hefty fee?!) and the very disappointing view at the top (the bushes hide any potential view!). But overall it's a very nice way to spend a morning. I say morning as the afternoon sun combined with the steep steps would make you lose your body weight in sweat. Go early. Or at sunset.
title: Nice Buddhist temple

body: I loved the bus ride to get to Mulkirigala as you get a real taste of rural Sri Lanka. The short walk to the cave temples from where you get off the bus is lovely and very peaceful. The temples at the various levels of terraces are very interesting and some of the paintings on the ceilings are gorgeous. Would highly recommend doing this trip. The monkeys are great too as you can watch them for ages while they feed :-)
title: A well worthwhile trip into rural Sri Lanka

body: There are around 500 steps going up to the top, so it's best to visit in the evening around 4pm if you don't want to expire! Interesting terraces with Buddhist cave paintings and some Hindu additions, as well as reclining buddha statues. This site is not in the best condition, but it is a working temple with resident monks, and still visited for full moon festivals by many local people. It's definitely worth a visit, and even though we had a guide, you don't really need one if you have a reasonable guide book.
title: Spectacular view from the top

body: Not a hard climb to the top. If you can make a coin rest on the shelf of the pagoda, you may make a wish! Walk on the outside of the fence down to the big rock - great view but take care!
title: Climb down on the rock!

body: Having visited many a temple one would think we would give another a miss. This one is worth it for the hill walk and the naugthy monkeys!!!
title: Monkeys galore!!!

body: Mulkirigala is a must see in a tropical forrest setting within high rocks which offer an incredible view of the area down to the sea. The enormous reclining buddhist sculptures set into decorative caves with hindhu adornments too are so atmospheric and we recommend you take the services of a local guide. Ours was fabulous and we also had a blessing at the last cave where we were given white wrist bands. We will never forget our visit there.
title: Stunning Rock Temple

body: Took a tuk tuk for 1500 rupees that waited for us while we finished. 30 minutes from Tangalle.It was noon and the visit took like 1:30h. Just one guy offered to be our guide and after we said no he did not insist. Indeed as exiting the multiple caves the man at every door kept asking for donation but as the ticket was 300 I think that was donation enough for a temple. The paintings were the most interesting part by far.And yes, incredibly as it may sound there were no monkeys!
title: No monkey and no monkey business

body: A great piece of hinduistic history. The whole place is fully worth visiting. In addition, there are tens of monkeys on the temple, which is a great bonuss to take some pictures with them.There are a lot of hard stairs, but when You got to the top, You see that the hard work (going the stairs) is worth it.
title: Worth visiting

body: The Rock structure of this temple is impressive and so are some of the paintings, however it is poorly maintained by the monks and there is little information for tourists.
title: Mulkirigala Rock Monastery

body: Buddha monastery and temple build in the high rock - with around 500 steps, picturesque view and plenty of monkeys in the trees. You can have a blessing and hear to the service.
title: Touch the Divinity of nature and Buddha

body: Quiet, calm and not crowded give a special atmosphere to this temple. Stunning views from the top. At this point, you're faced with spirituality and peace, no fuss. Painted walls of the temple and sculptures of Buddha is amazing.We were after sunset and got to the evening service, very impressive.The entrance ticket cost 300 rupees.
title: Quiet and beautiful temple

body: We've made one day trip from Tallala beach to Rekawa Lagoon, Mulkurigala, Blow Hole and Dickwella. The Monastery is a diamond of this trip. Google maps show good road to choose, if some questions - ask locals about TEMPLE and they will show the way. Upon arrival we bought about 6 lotus flowers from locals for about 20 rupees, which is a good price. Also some boy started to offer his service as a guide, he wanted 2000 rupees, we gave 500 for 2 person and I might say that we laughed a lot because he knows only about 20 words in English like toilet, Buddha sleeping, meditation, legs, eyes, elephant and repeats them in each room. So I suggest to walk around this beautiful place with professional guide or alone with guide book. You will enjoy beautiful views, incredible paintings and sculptures, feel the spirit of buddhism. Don't forget to take some water because you will have to climb lots of steps on the top.
title: GO! but don't hire a guide

body: This is a very old Buddhist monetary, You can see and study about the real Buddhism culture in Sri Lanka at this temple. There is a huge rock and at the top of the rock you can see the see 20-30 kms away. Fantastic location and good exersice
title: Great Budist monestry

body: Just for personal reasons. I have gone there as a child & thought i would do it again. It is always interesting for me to explore
title: Visitng After A Long Period

body: This is a Buddhist monastery 10 - 15 Km away from the Tangalle and don't forget to see this 250 years aged place
title: cant even believe

body: The temples carved into the rock aren't especially unique, but the old paintings are beautiful. The climb to the very top, however, is well worth it, with the crazy steps carved into the rock. At the top, the monk will give you a blessing for having reached the top, and take you around a path where you can see for miles and miles all around. Amazing view.
title: Nice walk, beautiful view

body: The place is nice, the rock monastery is interesting, but be prepared to pay for everything... For entry, for every floor (everywhere stands some money collector), for parking,...
title: Money for everything...

body: Really enjoyed our trip to the temple.Beautiful Buddhas and stunning painted ceilings.Nice to be away from crowds and feel the history.I regret not having purchased some small purchase from the old people selling books etc under the trees near the entrance as it didn't seem so many tourists came here.We had a great tuktuk driver ..a great day out.
title: A great experience

body: Not like Sigiriya. Not as spectacular. Some of the temples carved into the rock contains some interesting paintings. Worth a climb and a look if you happen to be in the area.
title: Exhaustive Climb up a Rock Temple

body: Really beautiful temple. Take a local guide at the entrance, it makes the experience so much more enriching and it is very cheap!
title: Definitely worth a visit

body: The artwork is interesting and the sites provides some interesting insights into the history of Sri Lanka. Be prepared for a steep climb climb though. 564 steps in total and they are all up!! Id recommend a morning viewing :)
title: Wroth the visit

body: We went there by yuk yuk and enjoyed the scenery there and back. Climbing up was a welcome workout after the eating and drinking.
title: Worth a visit.

body: Enjoyed the climb, and the triple blessings my son received. An enjoyable experience....be ready for a steep climb and take water.
title: Great trip out from Tangalle

body: Mulkirigala is more impressive and rich sightseeing then Dambulla. It's still not so commercially over rounded. Tickets for 600 LKR are a pleasant surprise too. The views from the top of the rock are just incredible. Paintings, sculptures and other religious objects even more rich, then in Dambulla. I'd advice to everybody who takes a stay in southern coast of Sri Lanka.
title: More empressive then Dambulla caves

body: amazing old temple , well i have been many srilanka temple , this was the best for me . other place they more in to taking money than showing you old temple , this was perfect temple feeling
title: amazing place

body: In fact, we arrive here a little bit late so the temple will be closed in half an hour... They close at 6:00 pm. We walk until the top (and there are so many stairs) and we could see some monkies, the view from the top and we offer some flowers (we bought it in the entrance) to Buddha... As it is suppose to do.We couldn't see the paintings (inside the rock) because the man who works there, said it was too late... 10 minutes to close... You have to walk without shoes but we felt good with this... It was good feel that you are more in contact with the Earth!!!
title: Good energy... Good for meditation... Great views.

body: Too bad I can't remember our guide's name, because he was a fountain of info. I do remember that he is 63 and used to work for the government before quitting to become a guide. :) At any rate, we learned many things about this fascinating place that we wouldn't have had we not hired such a good guide. We were at Tangalle for the beach, but this was a nice change from lolling about on the sand.For the record, contrary to other reviewers, I saw no touts or monkeys. Perhaps they did each other in! Well, unless you count the lady who asked if we wanted to buy some popcorn, but she was hardly pushy.Nobody harassed us to donate at the various shrines, either. There were donation boxes there but nobody said boo about them to me. We paid our admission fee and that was that. No pressure from anyone, and the guide we hired was well worth his fee.I did not check out the toilets so I can't speak to their level of revolting-ness (is that a word? Nah, that's not a word. Revoltivity? Revoltitude?) But I'm not a delicate flower about those things, and I've seen some pretty wretched public facilities back home in Canada, so I'm not about to complain when I see them here. Which I have not, as yet, on this trip.I didn't mind the climb to the top of the monastery but I'm fit, so it wasn't a problem. The cardiovascularly-challenged might want to think twice but really, if you take your time, you'll be fine. Our guide, as I mentioned, is 63 and he did just fine. And the views from the top are gorgeous.The paintings and statuary were quite lovely. There some amazing reclining Buddhas, and of course Buddha nirvana. It was helpful to have the guide explain many of the paintings and statuary to us.I'd say it's not quite as elaborate as Dambulla (which we visited in 2006) but still well worth visiting. Don't be afraid of touts and monkeys. Just go!
title: We had a very knowledgeable guide!

body: It was a beautiful temple. Quite the climb but very nice. Take water! It's a hot climb! The frescoes were quite freshly painted and very colorful.
title: A big climb but worth it

body: The temple is very interesting, the paintings and statues are beautiful but as is often the case a bit poorly presented with ugly lamp bulbs and behind dirty glass. The climb to the top is a must do. Visit in late afternoon to avoid heat.
title: Interesting, well worth a visit and stunning view

body: We went to Mulkirigala one afternoon from our hotel in Tangalle. I don't know what I was expecting, a mini Sigiriya perhaps, but I was disappointed. The rock itself and the monkeys that loiter upon it are definitely the highlights. The temples themselves look worse for wear and time has definitely taken its toll. The highest temple on the rock is no more than a shack with a rather odd looking ornament in it. Not worth the hike at all. The toilets at the siteare also revolting and there is nowhere to buy water or drinks, so make sure you stock up before you arrive.The other thing to watch out for is the people trying to scam you all over the place. We were charged a last minute parking fee for the tuc tuc that our driver seemed amused by, we had about 10 men follow us up the steps offering to be our guide, we paid the "foreigners" price to enter and were expected to donate to every temple on the rock.If you like monkeys, then this is worth to trip for that alone. But if you are looking to see a monastery in full swing or to see a beautiful temple that has been cared for over many years then go elsewhere!
title: Down trodden and full of scams artists

body: Beautiful and very authentic buddhist temple easily reached from Tangalle. Without hoards of tourist around, it leaves you feeling calm and in peace. Definitely a nice way of spending some free afternoon time
title: Good way of spending your afternoon

body: Fascinating rock carvings, painting and beautiful reclining Buddhas. View from the top is worth the steps.
title: Felt spiritual.

body: We had a great trip to Mulkiriglala and are so happy we decided to take the trip. The rock paintings are incredible, as our the sleeping buddhas. Even the drive out was very beautiful. A fabulous spot not to be missed!
title: What a find!

body: After some days on beach in Tangalle, we decided to visit this rock temple. We have not been in Dambulla, therefore we can't compare.We go there inthe afternoon by bus. The way took as about 1,5 hour. The bus is stopping everywhere. From the bus stop is easy walk for 15 minutes.We arrive to temple around 17, we bought tickets for 300 rp, each and enter. In the first level, there was puja.In the other floors, we were with 10 tourists. The stairs are realy high. But from the top, it is nice view. The best view is from rock behind the temple. At the top, in the right side, you will see the path way.
title: Hidden temple

body: Loved this temple and the superb 18th century reclining Buddhas. And with hardly anyone else, it was more enjoyable to admire the beauty of the statues and wall paintings. Didn't enjoy climbing up the steep stairs which seemed endless.
title: Majestic and beautiful - definitely worth visiting

body: It's almost as popular Dambulla, only without the crowds of tourists. Caves with sculptures ... beautiful view from the top. Be careful - a monkey can steal your stuff.
title: Temple in the jungle

body: Visited Rock temple while nobody was there and liked it very much. Many monkeys around and beautiful ancient paintings inside of the caves.
title: Exotic place with superb view

body: While we were in Tangalle we made a little trip to this rock temple and it was a really nice walk. After the gate there is a museum, a guy shows you around and naturally you need to pay him for his services so I did not go hehe. Just below the rock is a school for buddhist monks. You climb some stairs and get to the ticket office, the guy working there was really nice and there were people swiping and tiding up all the time. Of course when going into the little cave temple rooms you do need to follow temple etiquette.There are quite a few levels, at the top there is a dagoba and behind it (you need to go around the walls) there is a spectacular view! don't miss it.
title: Less touristy than Dambulla

body: This temple almost like Dambulla Temple and Sigiriya rock , our travel tip is going to Rock Temple morning time , before sun strong !
title: Great Excursion

body: The painted walls and huge Buddhas are very beautiful and I enjoyed our visit to Mulkirigala. Just after entering the main gate we were invited into a building and shown artefacts from the temples including ancient texts. I thought this was the ticket office, however after we received a weird Buddhist blessing from a man who was definitely not a monk we were asked for money for his services??? This was not so bad, just unexpected, and in hindsight rather funny. We then climbed a few more flights of stairs to find the real ticket office and commenced the hike up the hill looking in the various caves. TIP: wear walking shoes that slip on and off if you have them, shoes must be removed before entering each of the cave temples. ENJOY!
title: Interesting outing

body: One of the best sightseeings in Sri lanka. Four floors of beautifully decorated cave temples for only 200 rps per adult and 100 rps per student. Amazing value for money compared to the busier and overpriced sightseeings of the north such as Polonaruwa and Anaradhapura.
title: Excellent and refreshingly cheap sight

body: Huge granite rock which rises out of the surrounding forest. When you arrive its worth hiring a guide to explain the finer points but make sure he speaks good English (or whatever your language is). body: We were staying at Amanwella and the recommended to visit Mulkirigala. Their description did not compare to actually seeing it! Our tour guide, Ihsan, was knowledgeable about the monastery itself and its history. They warned us there were a lot of steps to climb - take this seriously! There are several levels as you climb up the mountain, each with a manmade cave full with beautiful paintings (the colors are still so vivid) and massive Buddha statues. There is even a chest where an important scroll was discovered that enabled them to decipher some ancient books about the history of Sri Lanka. Once we reached the very top the view was breathtaking! It's impossible to capture on camera. My recommendation is to wear sneakers or sturdy walking shoes and loose flowing clothing as there are hundreds of steps. And worth every one.
title: Breathtaking

body: I found full details of this amazing place in Rough Guide, and it sounded like a cross between Sigiriya and Dambulla. I was a bit sceptical about that, but it actually lived up to the hype! You approach it through a forested area, so it's quite a shock to suddenly see a huge grey rock looming high up way above the trees. It was Sunday, so the first thing I saw was several groups of children dressed in white, at Sunday School classes. This was a beautiful sight, and the children and teachers were happy to be photographed. Then we (myself and friendly tuktuk driver/guide), started up to the first level, and first rock temple. Very impressive, with Buddha images and wonderfully-painted walls and ceilings. More steps, and another level with even more to see, and after that, a third level! Finally to reach the very top, we climbed some incredibly steep tiny steps, more like a stone ladder. Actually we could have gone up by an easier staircase if we'd looked around, but the steep one was quite a thrill! On the very top of the rock there was just a ruined chamber and an enclosed bo tree, but the main interest was the amazing view in all directions. Well worth the climb, even for people not interested in temples! On the way down we were lucky enough to see some grey langurs, and then a very cheeky toque macaque who seemed to be striking a pose for my photos!
title: 0ver 700 steps, but so great that I didn't notice the pain!

body: I rate this rock temple more interesting than Dambulla - partly because it isn't crowded out with tourists. There seems to be a lot of money being spent on infrastructure near to the temple, so it is disappointing that many of the temples have been left in need of basic maintenance to stop water damage. The caves contain a mixture of 17th, 18th, and 19th century artwork styles. It is interesting to compare and contrast them. The climb to the final level is a challenge... try going up one way and back the other! When I got to the top there was not much of a view because of the height of the trees and the haze. This is another view point where it would have been better to get there in the early morning. Note that as long as you take off your shoes before entering each temple you do not have to leave them by the ticket counter. Climbing up the final wet steps without shoes could be quite dangerous.

body: I think the significance of this place could easily be overlooked. Fortunately, I didn't send the young man away who suddenly appeared and offered to guide me through the site. I would have enjoyed looking at the paintings on the walls and ceilings, the magnificent views out over the palm forrests and the climb to the top, but this very well-informed guy walked me through the history of the place and pointed out so many interesting stories depicted in the wall paintings. In one series, the five senses (sight, sound, etc.) was beautifully depicted in a style unique in all of Sri Lanka.One of the things I liked most about this beautiful place was the sense of solitude. I was the only visitor to the place at the time, and when my guide friend and I reached the top of the rock, it was so special to be able to have the stunning view all to myself.Although I had visited both Sigirya and Dambulla, and it is true that Mulkirigala is something of a mix between those two much better known sites, I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to this historically significant and very beautiful place.

body: We started our journey to Mulkirigala in the late afternoon, leaving bustling Tangalla behind we headed inland across some questionable roads, although to be fair there is huge road improvement in this area so it's just going to get better. The sights of rice fields with endless amounts of storks and buffalo, you get a great sense of real Sri lankan life. As we arrived a flurry of woman surrounded out Tuk-Tuk selling us beautiful flower arrangements as offerings for Lord Buddah. There were snacks and fresh hot tea on offer. The sun beginning to set so we hurried up the many steps to the three levels. Due to the time of day we could only visit the first level and the top level. Both of which offer various statues, paintings and incredible views of the area. Its a bit of a climb so to avoid a rush arrive by 3pm to really do it gracefully. I have to say we may have missed the second level caves but we saw a sunset at the top I will never forget. Its incredible. Have a hot cup of ginger tea once your back down and prepare yourself for a nail biting tuk-tuk ride as dusk turns to dark and the Sri Lankan bus service scares all.

body: Gosh, this was impressive. The guide spoke excellent English and gave us just the right amount of detail. He was prepared to answer questions if we wanted more information. The paintings were lovely. I liked the ones that had not been restored 300 years ago most, but they were all excellent. The reclining Buda’s are impressively. Perhaps the most surprising thing, is that when we arrived at 4pm we were the first tourists visiting that day. It is very atmospheric and being there on your own with the guide adds to that. It is hard to imagine that such an ancient monument is so far off the tourist trail. If you only visit one Buddhist site in Sri Lanka, I would recommend it is this one.

body: Mulgirigala is a rock monastery dated back to 2nd century B.C. There are few levels, to get to the highest one you will have to climbe 533 steps up the hill. The place is like a little prototype of Sigiriya, but with no tourists!!! The entrance fee is 200 Rupees per person. There are lots of monkeys on the first terrace. All in all a good place to visit if you are staying in Tangalle or in hambantota district.
